newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Exchange acts to end data delay problems.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Exchange acts to end data delay problems.

text.p: The Swiss Exchange said it was taking action to correct technical problems that have delayed data transmission to many traders and triggered complaints from banks and brokers alleging unequal treatment.

"We have had some problems in the past few days. I am speaking of delays between the central system and the SMF (Swiss Market Feed) system, purely internal delays," said one bourse official speaking on behalf of the exchange.
"We have activated workarounds, temporary solutions, that must ensure that soon we will no longer have this internal problem. We have taken action."
The official said the bourse had informed members about the measures it was taking.
"We are aware this is not the permanent solution, but a permanent solution needs more time," he added.
The steps follow complaints from traders that delays in price feeds were creating discrepancies in the market for shares and warrants and making dealing erratic.

"I have had delays of up to five minutes," one senior Swiss banker said. "We could not trade for days. It was very bad...The damage here is enormous, but it is not just the damage, but the aggravation."
An official at Martin Ebner's BZ group, who asked not to be identified by name, said swelling volume had created gaps between prices quoted on different systems.
He said the problems surfaced early this month as volume swelled and made efficient trading difficult.
"If you set an option price on an underlying asset where you have wrong prices, you can be 10, 20, 50 percent off. That costs money. It is a giant problem," the BZ official said.

The problems have hurt the exchange's image at a time it was regaining part of the trading volume that had moved offshore. Volume has soared as Swiss shares have posted the highest gains in Europe since the turn of the year.
The head of trading at another Swiss bank said the bourse had asked members to be patient and see if technical changes at the weekend could get trading back to normal by next week.

"We cannot go on like this," he said. "We have not lost any customers. They have shown some understanding that is is a phase we are going through, but it cannot last for three or four months. The EBS has told us that we should just wait for the weekend and see what happens."
